summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and alcohol dependence was admitted for chest pain, dyspnea, and an oral abscess after his medications were stolen. He developed acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation due to non-compliance, with pulmonary edema and volume overload, managed with IV diuresis and restarting home heart failure medications. His chest pain was determined to be non-ischemic, and he was restarted on metoprolol for atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate. An oral abscess was drained twice and treated with antibiotics. He showed signs of alcohol withdrawal, managed with symptom-triggered benzodiazepines, but left against medical advice with ongoing withdrawal symptoms. His kidney function declined mildly, likely due to diuresis, and he was discharged home with close follow-up instructions.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
